text:
Chris walked into the gym that day with the swagger of a man who had just watched one too many superhero origin stories. He spotted the new weight machine, a sleek beast of chrome and plastic, and decided it was time to prove he wasn't just there for the smoothie bar. With a confident nod to himself, he strapped in, assuming the position of a modern-day Hercules.

But the machine, it seemed, had other plans.

Instead of lifting, Chris found himself locked in a firm, unyielding hug with the equipment. He was stuck. His arms were pinned, his dignity was dangling by a thread, and he was frantically patting his own chest and the machine’s console, searching for a release button that seemed to have vanished into the ether. He looked less like a bodybuilder and more like a confused koala trying to escape a eucalyptus tree.

The nearby gym-goers didn’t offer help; they offered popcorn. Well, metaphorical popcorn. You could see the suppressed giggles rippling through the squat rack. One guy in a tank top actually wiped a tear from his eye. Chris, red-faced and humbled, finally found the little red lever, popped free, and walked away with the grace of a penguin on ice, vowing never to trust a machine that didn’t have a clear "I'm sorry" button.

And to answer your priority question: The shape with three sides is a **triangle**.
